news_drafts.headline: Blaenau Gwent draws £1.4m from reserves to cover spending overspend
news_drafts.lead: Blaenau Gwent dipped into its financial reserves during 2025/26 to cover an overall overspend against budget. The council drew £1.4m from its Financial Planning and Resilience reserves to fund an adverse variance, while specific reserves fell by a net £1.964m overall and school balances were reduced by £2.051m. Against this, the council's capital programme delivered at 86.2%, spending £41.1m of a £47.7m budget, with £6.5m of work carried forward into 2026/27. Four capital schemes recorded combined overspends of £80k, but these were accommodated within available resources. The council also secured £6.3m in new external funding for regeneration schemes in the final quarter, including £2.31m for Ebbw Vale Multi Storey car park refurbishment and £1.85m for Old Abertillery Library.

findings.committee: Corporate Governance and Resources Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: Council carries £10.55m in on-call lending facilities callable at lender discretion
findings.detail: Two facilities are structured on-call with no fixed repayment dates: £10m from Middlesbrough Teeside Pension Fund at 3.85% (taken December 2025) and £550k from BG & Caerphilly at Bank Rate (outstanding since June 2012). Lenders can demand repayment on these facilities at any time, requiring the council to immediately refinance or find cash.
findings.matters: Prospective lenders assessing the council need to understand its refinancing risk and potential immediate cash requirements if on-call facilities are called
findings.figures: £10.55m in on-call facilities; largest facility £10m at 3.85%; total outstanding borrowing £80.55m
findings.quote: 19/12/2025 MIDDLESBROUGH TEESIDE PENSION FUND CALL / VARIABLE 10,000,000 3.85 ON CALL

findings.committee: Corporate Governance and Resources Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: The council borrowed £8.8m via PWLB in March 2026 at rates of 4.29–4.31%, comprising a maturity loan and an EIP facility.
findings.detail: On 09/03/2026 and 06/03/2026, the council drew £3.8m and £5m respectively on new PWLB facilities at 4.29% and 4.31%. Both loans are shown as fully drawn with repayment scheduled for 2027–2029. This recent borrowing indicates the council is actively investing or has identified a financing need.
findings.matters: Recent borrowing decisions signal the council's capital investment plans and funding requirements; lenders will want clarity on purpose and revenue plans to service new obligations.

findings.committee: Corporate Governance and Resources Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: A PWLB maturity loan of £2.65m shows a repayment date of 16 June 2026, now three months overdue as of the report date.
findings.detail: The council borrowed £4m on 03/07/2001 at 5.13% with scheduled repayment on 16/06/2026. The loan still appears in the September 2026 schedule with an outstanding balance of £2.65m, suggesting the scheduled repayment date has passed. This could indicate an amortizing loan where interim payments have been made but final maturity has been missed, an undisclosed refinancing, or a data reporting lag.
findings.matters: A council showing scheduled debt obligations with past repayment dates and remaining outstanding balance is a credit concern; this requires explanation or remedial action.
findings.figures: Original value £4,000,000, current value £2,649,764.08, rate 5.13%, repayment date 16/06/2026

findings.committee: Corporate Governance and Resources Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: All borrowing is short-term from other councils and pension funds, at an average rate of 4.59%.
findings.detail: The schedule shows no PWLB or bond issuance: all £233m of borrowing is from other authorities and pension funds. Loans range from 1 to 184 days' duration. Interest rates across all borrowing average 4.59%, ranging from 4.0% to 6.1%. One facility from BG & Caerphilly (£550k) dated 2012 remains on-call at Bank of England base rate.
findings.matters: Short-term reliance creates refinancing risk. If market conditions tighten or lenders become less willing to roll facilities, the council faces pressure. A finance director would need to understand contingency plans and longer-term funding strategy.
findings.figures: Average Interest Rate 4.59%; total interest paid £3,142,857; rates range 4.0% to 6.1%

findings.committee: Corporate Governance and Resources Scrutiny Committee
findings.headline: The council raised £174.5m of temporary loans in 2025/26, with £75.55m still outstanding at 31 March 2026.
findings.detail: Borrowing brought forward from 2024/25 totalled £58.55m, of which £58m was repaid during the year leaving £550k outstanding. New loans of £174.5m were raised during 2025/26, of which £99.5m was repaid in the same year, leaving £75m outstanding. All borrowing is from other local authorities and pension funds. The pattern of £99.5m being raised and repaid within the same year indicates rolling short-term cash flow borrowing rather than permanent capital financing.
findings.matters: A lender needs to understand whether the council's £75.55m outstanding balance reflects a temporary cash shortfall or a structural funding gap, and whether there is a credible plan to reduce it. The scale and rolling nature of this temporary borrowing is material to credit assessment.
findings.figures: £174.5m raised in 2025/26; £99.5m repaid in same year; £75.55m total outstanding at 31/03/2026; £550k brought forward outstanding
